findings.finding: F1: The marker bytes rest on a precedent the repository contradicts: 1009-1070 keep the title's (/tmp/...) clause verbatim, 1010/1016 drop it, 997/998 had none; the two candidate lines are 44 vs 81 bytes and every byte-level check depends on the choice.
findings.answer: D1 (plan section 2): the title verbatim, clause kept, matching the main tip's own marker smoke/LEGSMOKE-1070.md and 1009/1021/1022/1056/1062/1063/1069. Constants frozen from the intended bytes: 81 bytes, 1 line, last byte 0a, sha256 d40b1d68fc7bad643b4f8b45579ca998478b6b8d0415a51b29ceab56b5f20bf5, blob 16c09df0dfeb9fdafa9f2ff4d748c9435030ef28. The implementer writes the file from the constant, never from the title, and stops and reports if its own sha256sum/wc -c disagree.

findings.finding: F2: The child spec is empty and the parent's acceptance names LEGSMOKE-1149, so whether the child's file names itself (Reading A) or the parent (Reading B) is a product choice the plan cannot settle alone.
findings.answer: I1 (section 1): Reading A - the child adds smoke/LEGSMOKE-1154.md naming LEGSMOKE-1154, as every prior child did (1069/1070, 998); the parent's clause is the parent's own marker. Recorded as the one specDeparture (the empty child spec gets Summary/Scope/Acceptance lines mirrored from the parent) and named in the completion summary for the architect to confirm or overrule; proceeding on I1 is the default.

findings.finding: F3: 'exactly one new file' is false at almost every head: no root .gitignore, so .legion/LEGSMOKE-1154/*.json rides the PR until retro removes it; a retro docs/solutions note would add a second merged file.
findings.answer: Section 4: A2 is Legion's diff from B with .legion/LEGSMOKE-1154/ excluded at H/H2 and every later head; unfiltered 'one file' only at R (A3) and M (A4). D3 (section 7.6, 9): retro writes no docs/solutions document (removal-only retro, allowed by skill://legion-retro line 125, precedent 998); if the architect wants one it is an accepted departure and A3/A4 list two files.

findings.finding: F4: Which push makes the head gate must be green on, and whether it is the approved head, is unsettled; the planner's usual first push is absent (handoff held locally) so firstCodeHead may coincide with the handoff; the ruleset's review requirements are unverified.
findings.answer: Section 4 names H (firstCodeHead = first pushed commit carrying the marker, recorded in implement.json), H2, R (retro's removal push, no trailer, starts gate) and M; A3 cites gate's pull_request run at R; the approved SHA comes from pulls/<n>/reviews (C4); step 7.7 re-reads rules/branches/main at merge time (P4). D4.

findings.finding: F5: compare/main...<head> names a ref that moves under the branch; status turns diverged on a sibling merge; the stop condition for a reset is undefined.
findings.answer: D2/P5 (sections 2-4): B=F=6d843f28 frozen; every Legion-diff read is compare/6d843f28...<sha> expecting status ahead (identical for the empty branch); anything else is a reset: stop, report to the architect, re-use no proof SHA. The literal compare/main form is reserved for the merge-time check A4 (commits/<M>) and is informational elsewhere; a moved main tip is normal.

findings.finding: F6: The appended line has no trigger, no bytes and a conditional criterion no machine can evaluate; it is unclear whether the reviewer may request it on its own or must wait for a targeted human message.
findings.answer: Section 6: the trigger is a targeted human message to the reviewer; the REQUEST_CHANGES review quotes the exact line, default L1 = 'Legion proof review round 1 (LEGSMOKE)' (line 2 of 24 markers); K=1 constants frozen (120 bytes, 2 lines, sha256 506140dbe49b3407d7220369ffe7628d593b5d78e687f7026cefb80755dcc6df, blob 42794032f145ade0f8854134ea8c78952eef8550); A5 is written as a branch (K=0: 1 line at R and M; K=1: exactly 2, sed -n 2p == L1) and the tester records which branch applied.

findings.finding: F7: Every measurement is a planning-time snapshot before an open-ended pause (the issue is itself an upgrade rehearsal); the plan must say which facts are frozen, which are re-measured, and what stops the run.
findings.answer: Section 2 freezes B=F, path, bytes, shas and the required-check reading; section 3 re-measures P1 (404 at ref=main), P2 (0 commits by path on main), P3 (PR list), P4 (ruleset contexts), P5 (compare/B...tip ahead) at every phase, with the stop rule 'P1/P2/P4 changed, a foreign PR, or P5 not ahead/identical -> do not push, report'; a moved main tip never stops the run. Section 9 names the cold-restart risk and that every needed number is in sections 2-5.

findings.finding: F8: Nothing in the repository verifies a Markdown marker; a green CI proves nothing about content (check is sleep 20); only gate is required; tooling constraints: od not xxd, read-only 404 controls, never a .fail-me probe, jq flags inside the filter, two check-runs per job.
findings.answer: Section 5: C1-C5 exact commands with expected outputs per head (contents API raw at SHA with wc -c/wc -l/od/sha256sum/head -1; compare from B filtered; git trees/blobs route for the tester; reviews commit_id + compare P...R + check-runs citing the pull_request pair; commits/<M> parents and files), od not xxd, mktemp -d outside the workspace, no probe file, flags inside the jq filter, 404 controls at B=F and ref=main.
